content: Dr. Kim Lindblade serves as the Head of the Elimination Unit within the Global Malaria Programme at the World Health Organization (WHO) in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Amanda Tiffany, an epidemiologist, is also part of the Elimination Unit at WHO. Dr. Li Xiao Hong works as a Technical Officer in the same unit, while Selome Tadesse provides assistance to the Elimination Unit. Laurent Bergeron is a Project Officer within the unit. Dr. Kevin Baird disclosed research support for a clinical trial involving tafenoquine combined with ACT for the radical cure of Plasmodium vivax. It was determined that this interest does not conflict with the meeting but would be disclosed to the Guideline Development Group (GDG) members. Professor Teun Bousema reported research funding related to evaluating the impact of mass drug administration (MDA) and mass testing and treatment (MTaT) on malaria transmission. This interest was also deemed non-conflicting but disclosed to the GDG. Professor Donicia Gamboa reported receiving research support from FIND Diagnostics as a co-principal investigator on a study validating a malaria rapid diagnostic test. This interest was determined not to conflict with the meeting but was disclosed. Dr. Marcus Lacerda disclosed research interests related to the use of tafenoquine, an 8-aminoquinoline, for the radical cure of P. vivax infections. This interest was similarly deemed non-conflicting but disclosed to the GDG. Dr. Kevin Marsh reported serving as an advisor to several organizations, including WHO, USAID, the Malaria Vaccine Initiative, and PATH. This advisory role was determined not to conflict with the meeting topics but was disclosed. Dr. Kamini Mendis, a Director on the Board of the Asia Pacific Leaders Malaria Alliance, authored a paper in 2019 discussing mass drug administration (MDA) as a tool for malaria elimination. Due to potential perceived bias, Dr. Mendis was recused from making judgments on MDA-related recommendations. Professor Melissa Penny declared financial research support received by her institute related to malaria elimination and broader malaria topics. This interest was deemed non-conflicting but disclosed. Dr. Allan Schapira reported being on the Board of Trustees of the UK-based charity Malaria Consortium. This role was determined not to conflict with the meeting but was disclosed. Dr. Chansuda Wongsrichanalai disclosed two interests: a paid consultancy with Medicines for Malaria Venture on radical therapy for P. vivax and travel/per diem support for attending international P. vivax meetings. These interests were deemed non-conflicting but disclosed to the GDG. The WHO Secretariat conducted due diligence, including online searches, to identify potential conflicts of interest among GDG members. Any identified conflicts were referred back to the members for updates to their declarations of interest (DOI). The declared interests were assessed by the WHO Secretariat, with support from the Office of Compliance, Risk Management, and Ethics as needed. Relevant declared interests and their management were summarized and disclosed to the GDG members. The WHO guidelines for malaria, updated on October 16, 2023, were developed following rigorous methodological standards. These guidelines are informed by evidence-based practices and aim to address key challenges in malaria control and elimination.
